name: Name
start_oid_tooltip: Leave it empty to use default interval
factor_tooltip: If you want to divide, use 0.1 or 0.01
difference_tooltip: The difference between two values will be used. Usefull for counters.
value2_tooltip: A second value shown in the circle, e.g. a battery state of charge (SoC in %)
without_card_tooltip: Draw the widget without the surrounding card (no background, no title)
widget_title_tooltip: Title shown in the header of the card
decimals_tooltip: How many decimals the values are shown with
devices_count_tooltip: Number of data points shown. One configuration group appears per device.
series_name_tooltip: Name shown in the legend and in the tooltip. Filled automatically from the object.
series_color_tooltip: Color of this series. Filled automatically from the object if it has one.
series_unit_tooltip: Unit shown next to the value. Leave empty to use the unit of the object.
sort_tooltip: Order the devices are drawn in
show_values_tooltip: Write the value next to each bar
stacked_tooltip: Stack the series on top of each other instead of drawing them next to each other
consumption_legend_tooltip: Show the names of the series above the chart
show_toolbox_tooltip: The small icons of the chart that switch stacking on and off and open the data table
consumption_oid_tooltip: Data point with a history: a counter (switch "Calculate difference" on) or an already aggregated consumption
comparison_oid_tooltip: Data point with the value of this device. It is read live, no history instance is needed.
comparison_type_tooltip: Bar chart for a ranking, pie chart for the shares of a whole
time_widget_tooltip: Interval selector widget this chart follows. Without it the period of the whole view is used.
interval_oid_tooltip: Data point with the length of the period: day, week, month or year
aggregate_tooltip: How the history instance condenses the raw values of one bar. For counters use "max" together with "Calculate difference".
percentile_tooltip: Percentile between 0 and 100 the history instance calculates
quantile_tooltip: Quantile between 0 and 1 the history instance calculates
integral_unit_tooltip: Time unit of the integral in seconds, e.g. 3600 for one hour
integral_interpolation_tooltip: How the history instance fills the gaps between two samples while integrating
no_animation_tooltip: Draw the chart at once instead of animating it
animation_duration_tooltip: How long one animation takes, in milliseconds
inner_radius_tooltip: Size of the hole in the middle, in percent. 0 draws a full pie.
inner_title_tooltip: Text in the middle of the ring, above the inner value
inner_oid_tooltip: Data point whose value is shown in the middle of the ring, e.g. the total
inner_unit_tooltip: Unit written directly after the inner value
legend_tooltip: List the devices with their values under the chart
legend_height_tooltip: How much of the height the legend takes, in percent
hide_labels_tooltip: Do not write the percentages into the segments
precision_tooltip: Decimals of the percentages inside the segments
show_period_tooltip: Whether this period gets a button. If none is selected, all four are shown.
hide_now_button_tooltip: The button that jumps back to the running period
date_format_tooltip: How the shown period is written
time_start_oid_tooltip: Optional data point the selected start of the period is written to, so that scripts and other views can read it
time_interval_oid_tooltip: Optional data point the selected length of the period is written to: day, week, month or year
default_color_tooltip: Color of the connection lines and circles that have no own color
nodes_count_tooltip: Number of circles around the house, in addition to the power line. One configuration group appears per node.
line_width_tooltip: Thickness of the circles and of the segments of the house ring, in pixels
distribution_no_animation_tooltip: Stop the moving dots on the connection lines. Saves processing power on weak devices.
raw_values_tooltip: Switch off the automatic conversion: a data point in Wh is otherwise shown in kWh, and a value without a unit gets "kWh" written after it
home_oid_tooltip: Data point with the consumption of the house, shown in the middle circle
text_color_tooltip: Color of the label. Empty uses the color of the theme.
standard_icon_tooltip: Icon from the built-in collection. Only shown while no own image is selected.
custom_icon_tooltip: Own image, uploaded or from the project. Replaces the standard icon.
units_tooltip: Unit shown after the value. Leave empty to use the unit of the data point.
round_tooltip: Decimals the value is rounded to
power_line_oid_tooltip: Data point with the power taken from the grid. A negative value means that energy is fed into the grid.
power_line_return_oid_tooltip: Separate data point for the energy fed into the grid, if it is not part of the power line data point
power_line_color_tooltip: Color of the grid circle while energy is taken from the grid
power_line_return_color_tooltip: Color of the value that is fed into the grid
node_oid_tooltip: Data point of this node, e.g. the PV production, the wallbox or the heat pump
hide_if_less_tooltip: Circles whose value is below this number are faded out in the view. Leave empty to always show them.
invert_direction_tooltip: Turn the direction of the moving dot around, for data points that count the other way
motion_speed_tooltip: The larger the number, the slower the dot moves at the same value
value2_unit_tooltip: Unit of the second value. Leave empty to use the unit of its data point.
self_sufficiency_show_tooltip: Self-sufficiency is the share of the consumption that did not come from the grid. Self-consumption is the share of the production that was used at home.
self_sufficiency_values_tooltip: List production, house consumption, grid import and grid export under the rings
self_sufficiency_unit_tooltip: Unit written after the listed values, e.g. W or kWh
ring_thickness_tooltip: Width of the ring in pixels
autarky_color_tooltip: Color of the filled part of the self-sufficiency ring
self_consumption_color_tooltip: Color of the filled part of the self-consumption ring
track_color_tooltip: Color of the empty part of the ring. Empty follows the theme.
production_oid_tooltip: Data point with what the PV system produces
single_grid_oid: One data point for the grid
single_grid_oid_tooltip: The meter delivers one value for both directions: positive is taken from the grid, negative is fed into it
grid_oid_tooltip: Data point with the grid balance: positive is taken from the grid, negative is fed into it
grid_import_oid_tooltip: Data point with what is taken from the grid
grid_export_oid_tooltip: Data point with what is fed into the grid
house_consumption_oid_tooltip: Optional. Without it the house consumption is calculated as production - feed-in + grid import.
battery_orientation_tooltip: Whether the battery symbol stands upright or lies on its side
soc_oid_tooltip: Data point with the state of charge in percent (SoC)
soc_factor_tooltip: Multiplier for the state of charge, e.g. 100 for a data point that delivers 0 to 1
separate_power_oids_tooltip: The inverter has one data point for charging and another one for discharging instead of one signed value
battery_power_oid_tooltip: Data point with the charging or discharging power. The sign is set below.
positive_is_tooltip: Inverters disagree about the sign of the battery power. Set here which direction a positive value stands for.
charge_power_oid_tooltip: Data point that is greater than zero while the battery is being charged
discharge_power_oid_tooltip: Data point that is greater than zero while the battery is being discharged
power_unit_tooltip: Unit of the power. "W" is converted to the capacity unit for the remaining time; every other unit is used as it is.
capacity_tooltip: Usable capacity of the battery. Needed for the remaining time and for the stored energy.
capacity_oid_tooltip: Data point with the capacity, if the inverter reports it. It wins over the fixed number above.
capacity_unit_tooltip: Unit written after the capacity, usually kWh
show_power_tooltip: Write the charging or discharging power under the state of charge, with an arrow for the direction
show_remaining_tooltip: Estimate how long the battery still charges or discharges at the current power. Needs the capacity.
use_thresholds_tooltip: Change the color of the filling at the two thresholds instead of always using the same one
low_level_tooltip: Up to this state of charge in percent the battery is drawn in the low color
medium_level_tooltip: Up to this state of charge in percent the battery is drawn in the medium color, above it in the high one
cost_source_tooltip: "Value of the data point" takes the number as it is - the data point itself has to hold the amount of the shown period. "Sum from the history" reads the period out of the history instance, which also makes the period selector work.
costs_time_widget_tooltip: Interval selector widget this widget follows. It decides the period of the history read and how the monthly base fee is spread.
currency_tooltip: Symbol written after every amount of money
energy_unit_tooltip: Unit of the energy amounts. The price is understood as price per this unit.
cost_decimals_tooltip: Decimals of the amounts of money
show_details_tooltip: List costs, base fee and revenue under the balance
show_energy_tooltip: Add the kWh the amounts were calculated from to the breakdown
cost_color_tooltip: Color of the balance when more has to be paid than earned. Empty follows the theme.
revenue_color_tooltip: Color of the balance when the feed-in is worth more than the consumption costs
energy_oid_tooltip: Data point with the consumed energy. With "Sum from the history" this is usually the meter reading.
price_tooltip: Price per energy unit, e.g. 0.30 for 30 cents per kWh
price_oid_tooltip: Data point with the current price, for a dynamic tariff. It wins over the fixed price above.
base_fee_tooltip: Fixed amount per month. It is spread over the shown period, so a day gets roughly a thirtieth of it.
feed_in_oid_tooltip: Data point with the energy fed into the grid. Leave empty if there is nothing to credit.
feed_in_price_tooltip: What one energy unit fed into the grid is paid with
feed_in_price_oid_tooltip: Data point with the current feed-in tariff. It wins over the fixed value above.
prices_oid_tooltip: Data point with the hourly prices as a JSON array, as tibberlink, awattar, epex-spot and similar adapters deliver it. A plain list of 24 numbers is read as the hours of today.
time_field_tooltip: Name of the field that holds the start of the hour. Leave empty, the usual names are recognized automatically.
price_field_tooltip: Name of the field that holds the price. Leave empty, the usual names are recognized automatically.
price_factor_tooltip: Multiplier for the prices, e.g. 100 to turn €/kWh into cents per kWh
hours_count_tooltip: How many hours are drawn. 0 shows everything the data point delivers.
only_future_tooltip: Leave out the hours that are over. If nothing is left, everything is shown anyway.
show_current_price_tooltip: Write the price of the running hour above the chart
show_average_tooltip: Draw a dashed line at the average of the shown hours
highlight_mode_tooltip: How the cheap and the expensive hours are picked out
highlight_rank: The n cheapest and most expensive
cheap_count_tooltip: How many of the cheapest hours are colored as cheap
expensive_count_tooltip: How many of the most expensive hours are colored as expensive
average_tolerance_tooltip: By how many percent an hour has to differ from the average to count as cheap or expensive
cheap_color_tooltip: Color of the hours that count as cheap
normal_color_tooltip: Color of all hours that are neither cheap nor expensive
expensive_color_tooltip: Color of the hours that count as expensive
current_color_tooltip: Color of the hour that is running right now. It wins over the highlighting.
no_prices: No prices found. Check the data point and the field names.
help_distribution: An animated diagram of where the energy flows: the house in the middle, the grid and up to ten more nodes around it, each with a dot travelling at the speed of its value.
help_consumption: One bar per hour, day or month of the selected period, read from a history instance. For meter readings switch "Calculate difference" on.
help_consumption_comparison: Compares the current values of several data points, as a ranking of bars or as the shares of a pie. Reads live values, no history instance needed.
help_interval_selector: Day, week, month or year, with arrows to step through the periods. The other widgets of this set follow it instead of carrying their own picker.
help_self_sufficiency: Two rings: how much of the consumption did not come from the grid, and how much of the production was used at home. Calculated from production, grid and house consumption.
help_battery: A battery filled to the state of charge, with the charge or discharge power and an estimate of how long it lasts at that power.
help_energy_costs: Energy times price, plus the share of the monthly base fee and minus the feed-in revenue, for the selected period.
help_dynamic_price: The hourly exchange price as bars, with the cheapest and the most expensive hours highlighted. Reads the JSON array of tibberlink, awattar, epex-spot and similar adapters.
